Summarize a multiScaleR fit

Source: R/print_methods.R
summary.multiScaleR.Rd

Summarizes a fit from multiScale_optim(): the estimated scales of effect with standard errors and intervals, the distances that contain most of each kernel's weight, and the fitted model at those scales.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
summary(object, profile = FALSE, dimension = c("2d", "1d"), ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class multiScaleR from multiScale_optim().

profile

Logical. If TRUE, report profile-likelihood confidence limits for sigma where feasible instead of Wald limits. Default: FALSE, which keeps summaries fast. See "Profile-likelihood intervals" below.

dimension

Character. "2d" (default) reports, as the selected distance, the radius that holds prob of the weight of an ideal kernel on a plane. "1d" restores the original distance along a line. Both definitions remain in the returned object and the printed output.

...

Optional arguments. prob, a number strictly between 0 and 1, sets the proportion of cumulative kernel weight used for the distances. Default: 0.9.

Value

An object of class summary_multiScaleR, a list that prints as a report. Its elements:

  • opt_scale: data frame with one row per optimized covariate and columns Mean (estimated sigma, map units), SE, 2.5%, and 97.5%. Its interval_method attribute records how each row's limits were found, such as "wald", "log_wald", "profile", or "unavailable". Profile limits that reach a search bound are labeled "profile_bound" by the default refit backend and "profile-bound-limited" by the analytic and joint mixed backends.

  • opt_shape: the same table for the shape parameter under kernel = "expow", otherwise NULL.

  • opt_dist_1d: distances in map units, with columns Mean, 2.5%, and 97.5%, at which a kernel's cumulative weight along a line through the point reaches prob (about 1.65 sigma for a Gaussian kernel at 90%).

  • opt_dist_2d: the radius, in map units and with the same columns, of the circle around the point that holds prob of the weight of an ideal, untruncated kernel on a plane (about 2.15 sigma for a Gaussian kernel at 90%).

  • opt_dist and opt_distance: two names for the distance table selected by dimension (2D by default, rather than the 1D definition used through version 0.7.3).

  • dimension: the selected definition, "2d" or "1d".

  • prob: the cumulative weight proportion used for the distances.

  • fitted_mod: the model refit at the estimated scales (opt_mod of the fit, or the native survival model inside an amt wrapper).

  • kernel: the kernel name.

  • hard_radius: names of covariates whose scale is a hard radius.

  • diagnostics, warn_message, next_run, call: copied from the fit; see multiScaleR.

  • backend: the backend name, present for the analytic and conditional-logistic backends.

Read the summary

Sigma is the kernel's scale parameter, and it is not itself a distance you can report. The distance tables translate it into the distance that holds 90 percent (by default) of the kernel's weight, which is usually the number to report as the scale of effect. Hard-radius covariates report their radius in both tables. See kernel_dist() and multiScaleR-kernels for when to use each definition and for the formulas.

Kernel-scale limits default to Wald intervals from the Hessian. For hard-radius landscape and unweighted surface metrics, and every radius estimated under kernel = "fixed", Hessian standard errors and Wald limits are shown as NA; use profile = TRUE for profile-likelihood limits. An error during profiling is reported rather than returning invalid limits.

Set dimension = "1d" to keep the original opt_dist and opt_distance values in existing scripts. For extraction that does not depend on the setting, use opt_dist_1d or opt_dist_2d. Neither choice changes the fitted sigma, coefficients, or likelihood. The 2D radius is for an ideal continuous kernel; max_D, raster edges, missing cells, and cell geometry can change the realized weight in the prepared data.

Profile-likelihood intervals

The default refit backend caches profile results during the current R session; the analytic and joint mixed backends recompute them. Set options(multiScaleR.profile_cache_max_bytes = 64 * 1024^2) to bound the retained cache entries (64 MiB by default), or set it to zero to disable caching and clear retained entries at the next profile request. Oversized entries and custom refits are computed without the cache. A failure to store a cache key warns and computes the same intervals directly, while numerical profile failures still raise errors. The returned refit scale table records cache availability in its profile_cache attribute. The option bounds retained entries, not temporary key construction or the memory used by the numerical profile.

Two kinds of fit have no profile intervals. For a fit with a declared radius_grid (see multiScale_optim()), profile = TRUE warns and returns the summary with the ordinary limits: NA for the hard radii and Wald limits, conditional on the selected radii, for any smooth scale. Inspect diagnostics(object)$radius_profile for the candidate likelihoods. For backend = "conditional_logit", scale uncertainty is not calibrated, so profile = TRUE warns and returns NA scale limits; use profile_sigma() to view the log-likelihood across sigma.

Analytic backends

For backend = "profile_glm" or "joint_nb2", default scale limits use joint information on the log scale and are omitted when the identifiability checks fail (see multiScaleR-fitting-methods). backend = "joint_mixed" reports the same log-scale Wald limits from its joint Hessian, one scale at a time. A returned Wald interval describes the local curvature around the selected optimum and can extend beyond the searched scale range. Coverage can fall below the nominal level even for an interior fit, so inspect the likelihood over the admissible range when scale inference matters.

With profile = TRUE, the analytic and "joint_mixed" summaries follow the connected likelihood region around the fitted scale, and an endpoint at a search bound is labeled bound-limited. A "joint_mixed" profile refits the native glmmTMB model at each candidate sigma and reports limits for every scale, including one whose standard error is withheld (see multiScaleR-fitting-methods). For a supported one-scale NB2 fit, scale_inference() checks the full range and reports the regions it detects. If a full-range profile suggests a competing optimum, compare additional starts, including both bounds. The printed coefficient summary still conditions on the estimated kernels; use vcov.multiScaleR() for the joint covariance.

See also

multiScale_optim(), print.summary_multiScaleR(), profile_sigma(), kernel_dist(), and vignette("v09-estimates-and-intervals", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

data(pts)
data(count_data)
hab <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "hab.tif",
                               package = "multiScaleR"))
inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts, raster_stack = hab, max_D = 250,
                      kernel = "gaussian", verbose = FALSE)
fit <- multiScale_optim(glm(y ~ hab, family = poisson, data = count_data),
                        inputs, verbose = FALSE)
s <- summary(fit)
s$opt_scale     # sigma with Wald limits, in map units
#>         Mean       SE     2.5%    97.5%
#> hab 76.16637 9.567451 57.09847 95.23428
s$opt_dist_2d   # radius holding 90 percent of the kernel weight
#>       Mean   2.5%  97.5%
#> hab 163.45 122.53 204.37

# Profile-likelihood limits instead of Wald limits
summary(fit, profile = TRUE)$opt_scale
#>         Mean       SE     2.5%    97.5%
#> hab 76.16637 9.567451 59.86998 99.38553
